title: Adaptive LTS lanes and emergency rollback operator for runtime upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket defines and implements an operational policy and supporting automation for adaptive LTS lanes plus an Emergency Rollback Operator to minimize customer disruption during runtime upgrades. Goal: enable frequent safe upgrades (minor and patch releases) while providing a fast, tested escape hatch for any release that causes regressions in latency, correctness, or cost economics.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc published with LTS lane definitions, promotion rules and canary gate thresholds (Confluence link in links)
Release Operator CRD implemented to orchestrate channel promotions and image rollouts (controller + RBAC + tests)
Emergency Rollback Operator implemented that can: shift traffic away, pin runtime image versions, restore KV cache markers, and orchestrate cache warmup on previous image
Automated post-deploy verification hooks integrated into the rollout pipeline: perf p99, 5xx rate, token cost delta, and eval-suite quality score must be recorded and enforced
Compatibility scoring integrated into the migration assistant; score >= 90 required for automatic promotion from experimental -> stable-long LTS
Runbook and playbooks added to Ops playbooks repo with step-by-step rollback procedures and Slack alerts
Two end-to-end canary rollouts executed in staging and one dry-run in production with simulated failure to validate rollback operator
decisions: Adopt three release lanes: experimental (daily), stable (weekly minor), stable-long / LTS (quarterly with 12-18 month support)
Promotion requires passing automated quality gates and compatibility score threshold; manual override allowed for P0 customer hotfixes
Use controller-based Release Operator (K8s CRD) vs. bespoke scripts to centralize rollout logic and allow observability hooks
Rollback operator will own stateful steps (traffic shift, image pin, cache reconciliation) and must be able to run in cross-region mode
tradeoffs: Operator CRD centralizes logic but increases cluster surface area and RBAC complexity
Strict automated gates reduce risk but increase friction for urgent fixes — manual override policy balances speed vs safety
Cache reconciliation increases rollback time (warmup) but reduces cold-start flakiness for clients — acceptable for high-customer-impact rollbacks
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (design): finalize LTS lane definitions and gate metrics; write Confluence design doc; 1 week
Phase 2 (operator): implement Release Operator CRD and Emergency Rollback Operator in controllers repo; unit + e2e tests; 3 sprints
Phase 3 (automation): wire operators into CI/CD pipeline; create post-deploy verification hook library; 2 sprints
Phase 4 (validation): run staged canaries in us-east-1 and eu-west-1; simulate failures and exercise rollback operator; 1 sprint
Phase 5 (launch): enable adaptive lane promotions on a subset of customer slices, monitor for 2 weeks, expand
rollback_playbook: Alert received: rollout triggered high-regression alarms (p99 > baseline + 30% or eval-quality delta > 5%)
Run automated rollback command: kubectl release rollback <release-cr> --strategy emergency

Rollback Operator steps: 1) set trafficWeight to previous image via TrafficSplitter, 2) pin node images using imageOverride annotation, 3) set KV cache marker key 'runtime:migration:active' to previous-version, 4) trigger cache warmup job
Notify customers with status page update and per-tenant rollback notes (templates in runbooks)
Postmortem: create incident ticket, collect logs/traces, compute regression root cause, propose mitigation in next release
testing_checklist: Unit tests for operator reconciliation loops
Integration test for promotion / demotion paths including DB and config updates
Chaos test that toggles 10% of requests to simulated failures during canary
Quality regression test: run eval-suite against canary and baseline models
Performance regression test: synthetic traffic replicating 95th/99th percentile sequences
End-to-end dry run of emergency rollback in staging with simulated KV state changes
review_feedback: PM review (Jordan Li): prefer explicit tenant opt-in for experimental lane; reduce blast radius by percentage-of-traffic gating
Security review (Nora Kim): ensure CRDs only writable by release-bot service account; KMS access must be audited
Design review (Lena Gomez): add compatibility score telemetry to console and expose consumer-level migration warnings
SRE (Tom Becker): require synthetic traffic golden requests to be included in post-deploy checks to catch correctness regressions
next_steps: Finalize canary gate numeric thresholds and add to design doc
Create initial Release Operator CRD spec and start implementation branch
Schedule cross-team review with SRE, Security, and SDK owners in next planning meeting
Build migration assistant export that computes compatibility score for top 100 customers
